static_defect_verified_against_the_store.author_verification: sharper than that, checked against the committed worker_manager/store.py. transact (line 775) calls replay (line 943) and RETURNS the recorded value when the row exists with a MATCHING signature (lines 795-807), so an exact replay never raises at all. replay raises operation-collision ONLY when the row exists with a DIFFERENT signature or kind (lines 969-975). And _identity (line 192) deliberately excludes the runtime from the operation id -- documented, citing attempts.start_failure_operation_id -- precisely so the runtime and correlation ride the SIGNATURE. Therefore operation-collision on this path means exactly one thing: a durable intent exists for this act and it describes DIFFERENT operands. So the branch grants authorization in the ONE case where the durable record provably does not describe the effect about to be ordered, and the docstring's "A COLLISION SATISFIES THIS ... Replay stays honest" is inverted -- replay is handled by the success path. _same_account already exists in the file and is applied to the outcome chain; it was not applied here.
